notes: Normalized 2026-07-23 from the free-text verdict 'yes (provisional) for the declared-modifier-recoverable band; a residual sub-band routed to owner'. The matrix makes the verdict binary, so the qualification moves here rather than into the verdict.

The provisional qualification, preserved: the band is recoverable by declaring the matching minlength/maxlength on the source of the assigned expression, which is an ordinary modifier available at every occasion. The residual sub-band the original author routed to the owner is an assigned expression whose length cannot be bounded by declaring anything on its sources — the candidate is an interpolated string over an unbounded numeric hole. Corpus measurement decides whether that residual is non-empty; the verdict does not ratify on this argument alone.

dischargeContract.derivation: The obligation discharges IFF StringLengthIntervalOf(RHS) yields [min, max] with max.HasValue and min >= declaredMinLength and max <= declaredMaxLength.
dischargeContract.decisionProcedure: Computes a static character-length interval [min, max?] for the assigned string RHS via StringLengthIntervalOf (ProofEngine.Lengths.cs:55-128) — literal -> exact point (len,len); field/arg reference -> its declared [minlength, maxlength] with notempty folding min to >=1; concatenation -> operand-interval sum; conditional -> branch union; length-stable string function -> argument transfer; interpolated string -> literal-segment + per-hole sum. Discharge is prove-or-reject: proved iff the whole interval is provably within [declaredMinLength, declaredMaxLength] (min >= declaredMin AND max.HasValue AND max <= declaredMax); a provable violation (false) OR a merely-unprovable case such as an unbounded upper bound (null) both leave the obligation Unresolved and emit LengthBoundViolation (spec 0.7 prove-or-reject, no runtime deferral).

An arg-length fact is earned at phase 1 (ingress governance) and is never killed (nothing in a plan writes an argument), so it reaches the write on every route carrying the event including the inspect-fire mirror (transport rule, section 5, 'Ingress-governed argument fact'). A field-reference fact is a carried modifier fact earned at route position zero, killed only by an ungoverned write to that field between position zero and the site (transport rule route-indexed frame-and-kill, section 4). A literal read-closure is empty and is never killed."
